frameworksData.heading: Grounded in the frameworks that make learning work.
frameworksData.description: Every build rests on established instructional design, learning experience design and adult learning science, not guesswork.

items.name: ADDIE
items.description: ADDIE is the most widely used instructional design process in the world. Each phase feeds the next, so nothing is built until the need, the audience and the objectives are clear, and every output is measured against them.

usage.label: How Edstellar uses it
usage.text: We run ADDIE for structured, high-stakes programs where scope, sign-off and auditability matter.

items.name: SAM
items.description: The Successive Approximation Model replaces ADDIE's linear path with rapid cycles of prototype, review and refine. Stakeholders see working content in days, not months, and shape it as it is built.

usage.label: How Edstellar uses it
usage.text: We use SAM when speed and stakeholder feedback matter more than a fixed upfront spec.

items.name: Adult learning principles
items.description: Andragogy, Malcolm Knowles' theory of how adults learn, is why our content respects the learner. Adults need to know why, bring real experience, and learn best when the content solves a problem they have right now.

usage.label: How Edstellar uses it
usage.text: Every module is built problem-first and tied to the learner's real work, never theory for its own sake.

items.name: Bloom's Taxonomy
items.description: Bloom's Taxonomy classifies learning objectives by cognitive complexity, from recalling facts to creating new work. It keeps objectives honest, so content that claims to build judgment actually practices it.

usage.label: How Edstellar uses it
usage.text: We write every objective at the right level, then design activities and assessments to match.

items.name: Gagné's Nine Events
items.description: Gagné's Nine Events of Instruction is the lesson-level blueprint for how people take in, process and retain information, from gaining attention to transferring it to the job.

usage.label: How Edstellar uses it
usage.text: Each lesson is structured around these events, so attention, practice and retention are designed in, not left to chance.

items.name: Merrill's First Principles
items.description: Merrill's First Principles distills decades of instructional research into five that consistently drive results: learning happens when real problems are tackled, prior knowledge is activated, and skills are demonstrated, applied and integrated into the work.

usage.label: How Edstellar uses it
usage.text: We pressure-test every design against these five principles before a single asset is built.

items.name: Kirkpatrick's Four Levels
items.description: The Kirkpatrick Model is the global standard for evaluating training. It moves measurement beyond “did they like it” to whether behavior changed on the job and the business improved.

usage.label: How Edstellar uses it
usage.text: We baseline and measure at the levels that matter to your goals, usually behavior and business results.

items.description: The 70-20-10 model reflects how capability is really built: mostly through challenging work, some through others, and a focused share through formal content. It keeps courses in proportion to practice and coaching.

usage.label: How Edstellar uses it
usage.text: We design formal content to trigger and support the 90% of learning that happens on the job.
